claims.label: Neff/Boring Joint Podcast Announced via Promotional Materials
claims.claim: Blake Neff and Jeremy Boreing released promotional photo and audio/video promo clip announcing a joint podcast sitdown.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain the full released episode and compare its content against Sausalito's pre-release predictions and the host's commentary.

claims.label: Sausalito Predicted Podcast Content Pre-Release
claims.claim: Bobby Sausalito predicted, prior to release, that the Neff/Boring podcast would primarily consist of criticism of Candace Owens and Tucker Carlson, defense of TPUSA figures (Erica Kirk, Mikey McCoy, Frank Turek), and calls for lawsuits/jail time against the host.
claims.investigative_direction: Compare Sausalito's specific predictions against the released episode segment-by-segment.

claims.label: Host Concurs Sausalito's Predictions Were "Almost Spot On"
claims.claim: The host explicitly concurs that Sausalito's pre-release predictions were "almost spot on" relative to the released promo clip.
claims.investigative_direction: Document the host's specific concurrence with each item of Sausalito's prediction list once the full episode is available.

claims.label: Neff Characterized Candace Owens as "Malicious, Hateful, Dishonest, Destructive"
claims.claim: In the Neff/Boring promo clip, Blake Neff stated that Candace Owens is a "malicious, hateful, dishonest, destructive actor in American life."
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain full Neff/Boring episode to confirm statement context and surrounding statements.

claims.label: Neff Stated Candace Wants Kirk's Killer to "Get Away With It"
claims.claim: In the Neff/Boring promo clip, Blake Neff stated that Candace Owens "wants the person who killed Charlie to get away with it."
claims.investigative_direction: Verify exact quote and context in the full Neff/Boring episode.

claims.label: Neff Asserted Tucker Carlson "Extended Maximum Grace" to Candace
claims.claim: In the Neff/Boring promo clip, Blake Neff stated that Tucker Carlson "has extended maximum grace to Candace Owens."
claims.investigative_direction: Verify exact quote and context in the full Neff/Boring episode.

claims.label: Boring X Post Claimed Owens Acts for Fame
claims.claim: Jeremy Boreing posted on X that Candace Owens "does this largely on purpose" and that "all Candace cares about is fame and money. Nothing is beneath her."
claims.investigative_direction: Retrieve the original post via web archive to confirm exact wording and timestamp.

claims.label: Loomer X Post Claimed Save America Act Would Not Pass Before Midterms
claims.claim: Laura Loomer posted on X that the Save America Act would not pass before midterms and projected poor GOP midterm outcomes.
claims.investigative_direction: Retrieve the original post via web archive to confirm exact wording and timestamp.

claims.label: Mitchell X Post Characterized GOP as "Genuinely Useless"
claims.claim: Jamie Mitchell posted on X that "The GOP is genuinely useless" and that Democrats were projected to sweep the midterms.
claims.investigative_direction: Retrieve the original post via web archive to confirm exact wording and timestamp.

claims.label: Libs of TikTok X Post Cited 59% Democrat Sweep Projection
claims.claim: Libs of TikTok posted on X that prediction markets project Democrats at a 59% chance of sweeping both chambers of Congress in the 2026 midterms.
claims.investigative_direction: Retrieve the original post via web archive to confirm exact wording, timestamp, and the specific prediction market referenced.

claims.label: Vance Clip Asked Voters for "Another Chance" Citing Policy Achievements
claims.claim: In a clip the host plays, JD Vance asks voters to "give us another chance" and lists tax cuts (overtime, Social Security, tips), success on the border and immigration, and H-1B reform as accomplishments.
claims.investigative_direction: Identify the original venue/date of the Vance clip to anchor sourcing.

claims.label: Host Says Two Grey Dodge Challengers Arrived on UVU Campus Within About 20 Minutes of One Another
claims.claim: The host says footage shows two separate grey Dodge Challengers arriving on the UVU campus within approximately 20 minutes of each other on Sept 10, both remaining on campus for roughly an hour and a half before departing near-simultaneously.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain parking-garage entry/exit logs and timestamped surveillance footage to independently verify the arrivals of two distinct grey Challengers.

claims.label: Host Says "Waluigi" Vehicle Driver Made Multiple Parking Attempts in Empty Lot
claims.claim: The host says the footage shows the driver of the second grey Dodge Challenger (code-named "Waluigi") making over three to four parking attempts in the empty admin/admissions lot before parking.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain the original admin-lot surveillance footage to verify the number of attempts and any identifying characteristics of the driver.

claims.label: Host Says "Maroon Boy" Vehicle Parked at Top of UVU Structure for About 8 Minutes Before Relocating
claims.claim: The host says the footage shows the grey Dodge Challenger associated with the "Maroon Boy" being driven to the top level of the UVU parking structure and remaining stationary there for approximately eight minutes, after which the subject relocated the vehicle to a lower level.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain the full top-of-structure surveillance footage to verify the eight-minute duration and any subject activity during that window.

claims.label: Host Says TMZ Footage at 8:07 AM Shows Robinson Already Parked Off Campus
claims.claim: The host says TMZ surveillance footage timestamped 8:07 AM on Sept 10 shows Tyler Robinson walking toward the UVU campus, and that this indicates he was already parked off campus at that time.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain the original TMZ footage with intact timestamps and any associated location metadata to independently confirm the timestamp and subject identification.

claims.label: Sept 15 Warrant Narrative Stated 8:28 AM Entry and 8:28–9:24 AM Wooded-Area Visit
claims.claim: The September 15 search warrant narrative (attributed to Agent Mortensson's review of UVU security video) stated that Robinson's Challenger entered the UVU parking structure at approximately 8:28 AM, that Robinson then visited a wooded area near where the rifle was later discovered, and that Robinson left the structure at approximately 9:32 AM.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain the actual Sept 15 search warrant filing to verify the quoted language and its full surrounding narrative.

claims.label: Host Alleges Hull Preliminary Hearing Testimony Omitted the 8-Minute Top-of-Structure Stop and Revised the On-Campus Timeline
claims.claim: The host alleges that Agent David Hull's preliminary hearing testimony presented a campus timeline in which the "Maroon Boy" interacts with a TPUSA representative, departs, and returns on foot, omitting the approximately 8-minute top-of-structure stop and the 8:28-9:24 AM wooded-area visit described in the Sept 15 warrant she reads.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain the preliminary hearing transcript and audio/video to verify the specific omissions and re-orderings between the warrant narrative and Hull's testimony.

claims.label: Miss Noble Testimony Described Dodge Challenger with Bald Driver and Two Backseat Occupants
claims.claim: Neighbor Miss Noble and her husband reported observing a Dodge Challenger being driven by a bald person with two people in the back seat, parked in their neighborhood shortly after Officer Go forth's sighting.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain Miss Noble's interview transcript, witness statement, or sworn testimony to verify exact wording and to determine whether the Dodge Challenger identification was confirmed via plate or visual match.

claims.label: Host identifies show community as Decentralized Intelligence Agency
claims.claim: The host states that the show / audience operates as the Decentralized Intelligence Agency (or close variant), a crowd-sourced tip network opposing centralized intel.
claims.investigative_direction: Preserve as brand / network framing claim; cross-link M-12 meme occurrence when present.
claims.transcript_snippet: ...can buy a mug. You can buy a CIA hat. We are the Decentralized Intelligence Agency. And we have a lot in store. Some stuff I am, of course, saving. I got lawsuits going on and lawsui...

claims.label: CIA hat merch framed as Candace / Decentralized Intelligence Agency brand
claims.claim: The host plugs CIA-branded merch (hat/line) and glosses it as Candace Intelligence Agency and/or the Decentralized Intelligence Agency twin brand.
claims.investigative_direction: Confirm on-screen merch graphic if available; reuse M-14 when exact Candace Intelligence Agency phrase airs.
claims.transcript_snippet: ...buy a Santa Cup. You can buy a mug. You can buy a CIA hat. We are the Decentralized Intelligence Agency. And we have a lot in store. Some stuff I am, of cour...

claims.label: Host Says Tucker Carlson Urged Looking at the Neff–Boreing Photo
claims.claim: The host says Tucker Carlson commented on the Blake Neff and Jeremy Boreing promotional photo by saying to just look at the photo.
claims.investigative_direction: Locate Carlson's original post or remark about the photo and confirm his wording and date.
claims.transcript_snippet: Tucker Carlson said, just look at the photo.

claims.label: Host Says Viewers Report the Towed Challenger Body Differs From the Admin-Lot Challenger
claims.claim: The host says car-knowledgeable viewers emailed that the body of the Dodge Challenger that was towed and identified as Tyler Robinson's differs from the Dodge Challenger shown in the administrative lot.
claims.investigative_direction: Compare the towed vehicle's make, year, trim and body photographs with the admin-lot footage frames, ideally with an independent automotive identification.
claims.transcript_snippet: there is a difference in the body on the Dodge Challenger uh which was towed and has since been identified as Tyler Robinson's Dodge Challenger

claims.label: Host Says the Second Challenger's Driver Has Exceptionally Tall Legs
claims.claim: The host says the person operating the second Dodge Challenger, whom she names Waluigi, has exceptionally tall legs and a body shape she uses as an identifying trait.
claims.investigative_direction: Measure the driver's proportions in the admin-lot footage against known heights of persons of interest, if the original footage is released.
claims.transcript_snippet: And he has exceptionally tall legs and he looks to me like he's shaped like Waluigi.

claims.label: Host Says the Two Challenger Drivers Are Not the Same Person
claims.claim: The host says she is not claiming the two Challengers are the same car and that she believes the person leaving the admin-lot Challenger is not the person in the parking garage at the same time; Challenger one is tied to the garage and Challenger two to the admissions lot.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain simultaneous timestamps from the garage and admin-lot cameras to show whether both subjects were on camera at the same moment.
claims.transcript_snippet: We do not think that the person who gets out of this car is the same person that is in the garage at the same time.

claims.label: Host Says Nobody Knows What Either Driver Did for About an Hour and a Half
claims.claim: The host says that no one has any idea what either Maroon Boy or Waluigi did during roughly an hour and a half on campus, and that no narrative has been provided for that time.
claims.investigative_direction: Request the full UVU campus camera archive for 8:30 to 10:00 a.m. covering both vehicles and their occupants.
claims.transcript_snippet: we have actually no idea what either of these two people did for an approximate hour and a half on campus

claims.label: Host Says the Hearing's Only Account of Maroon Boy Is Asking a TPUSA Employee About the Event
claims.claim: The host says that from the preliminary hearing the only thing known about Maroon Boy is that he parked, went up to a Turning Point USA employee and asked whether this was where the event would be held.
claims.investigative_direction: Read the preliminary hearing transcript for Hull's testimony on the TPUSA representative exchange and identify the employee asked.
claims.transcript_snippet: All we got from the pre preliminary hearing is that Maroon Boy parked went up to a Turning Point USA employee and asked her if this is where the event was going to be held.

claims.label: Host Says Her Timeline Error Came From Mixing Warrant Data With Hull's Testimony
claims.claim: The host says yesterday's timeline wrongly showed Maroon Boy visiting a wooded area during that window because her producer entered data from the September 15 search warrants while she used Agent David Hull's preliminary hearing testimony.
claims.investigative_direction: Compare the show's published timeline against both the September 15 warrant narrative and the hearing transcript to document which source supplied each entry.
claims.transcript_snippet: Yesterday, we wrongly showed you on the timeline um that this was during a time where he then went and visited a wooded area off campus.

claims.label: Host Says Maroon Boy and Waluigi Left Campus Around the Same Time
claims.claim: The host says Maroon Boy left campus in the Dodge Challenger at 9:33 a.m., around the same time Waluigi left, with the second departure placed about 17 minutes later at about 9:50.
claims.investigative_direction: Pull garage exit and admin-lot exit camera timestamps for both vehicles to confirm the near-simultaneous departures.
claims.transcript_snippet: he's going to leave 17 minutes later at about 9 9:50

claims.label: Host Says Hull Never Suggested the Challenger Was Tracked Off Campus
claims.claim: The host says the only Challenger footage the prosecution shows runs from about 8:30 to 9:33 a.m., and that Agent Hull does not suggest investigators tracked Maroon Boy's Challenger off campus or saw him change outfits.
claims.investigative_direction: Check the hearing transcript for any testimony on tracking the Challenger after 9:33 a.m. and for any off-campus license-plate-reader hits.
claims.transcript_snippet: Agent Hull doesn't even so much as try to suggest that they tracked Maroon Boy Dodge Challenger off campus.

claims.label: Host Says No Photo or Video Shows an Identifiable Challenger Parked Off Campus
claims.claim: The host says the prosecution has presented no photos or videos of an identifiable Dodge Challenger parked off campus, so linking the garage car to the person who later returned in a black shirt is assumption.
claims.investigative_direction: Search discovery and neighborhood camera releases for any frame of the Challenger parked near campus on September 10.
claims.transcript_snippet: There are no photos or videos of an identifiable Dodge Challenger parked off campus.

claims.label: Host Says Officer Goforth's Encounter With the Challenger Has No Indicated Bodycam
claims.claim: The host says prosecutors have never indicated there is body camera footage of the Dodge Challenger that pulled up to Officer Goforth after midnight and had a conversation with him.
claims.investigative_direction: Request Goforth's bodycam and dispatch records for the after-midnight contact and confirm whether any recording exists.
claims.transcript_snippet: They've never indicated that he had on body cam footage.

claims.label: Host Says Hull's Narration Sometimes Conflicted With the Footage Shown
claims.claim: The host says Hull's testimony over the surveillance footage was rapid and rehearsed, and that at times what he said and what viewers saw were in conflict.
claims.investigative_direction: Compare Hull's narration line by line with the released footage and note each point where the spoken description and the video disagree.
claims.transcript_snippet: at times we went back and realized those two things were in conflict with one another

claims.label: Host Says Zoomed Garage Footage Shows the Subject's Head Dropping Once
claims.claim: The host says that when she zooms in on the eight minutes at the top of the parking structure she sees only one moment when the subject's head goes down, which she suggests may be him picking up something near his feet.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain the full eight-minute top-level garage footage at native resolution for independent frame review.
claims.transcript_snippet: there's only one time where I observe what and I'm going to show you that what looks to me like he's I don't know maybe picking up something down by his feet

claims.label: Host Says the TMZ Footage Was Omitted From the Prosecution Presentation
claims.claim: The host says the TMZ footage showing Robinson earlier, already parked off campus at 8:07 a.m., was for some reason omitted from the prosecution's presentation and not raised in court.
claims.investigative_direction: Check the preliminary hearing exhibit list and Hull's testimony for any use of the TMZ 8:07 a.m. footage.
claims.transcript_snippet: The TMZ footage, which they, for some reason, omitted, actually shows him earlier.

claims.label: Host Theorizes the Garage Stop Was Staged to Capture the Challenger on Camera
claims.claim: The host speculates that the top-of-garage episode was done because the Dodge Challenger needed to be captured on camera at a specific pre-planned time, and says there is no reason Robinson could not have parked off campus all day.
claims.investigative_direction: Establish who selected the parking structure and arrival time, using Robinson's phone location data and campus gate or parking records.
claims.transcript_snippet: they needed that crucial footage of the Dodge Challenger captured onto camera at a specific pre-planned time

claims.label: Host Says the Maroon Boy Was a Decoy Whose Job Was to Be Filmed
claims.claim: The host says the car was meant to be seen and that the decoy boy's job was to make sure the Challenger was captured on camera throughout the parking structure.
claims.investigative_direction: Identify who drove the Challenger into the structure and test the decoy theory against Robinson's phone, purchase and message records.
claims.transcript_snippet: That was the decoy boy's literal job was to make sure that this car gets captured on camera throughout the parking structure.

claims.label: Host Says Her Show Broke the Dairy Queen Sighting and the Cemetery Clothes Story
claims.claim: The host says her show broke the story that Tyler Robinson was seen at a Dairy Queen and that he was reportedly throwing out clothes in a nearby cemetery, a story she says has never been formally addressed or denied.
claims.investigative_direction: Search the cemetery and nearby trash receptacles for records of recovered clothing and obtain Dairy Queen camera footage and receipts.
claims.transcript_snippet: we broke the story that Tyler Robinson was seen at the Dairy Queen and what was communicated was that he was throwing out clothes in the cemetery nearby

claims.label: Host Says Robinson May Be Guilty of Tampering but Not the Killing
claims.claim: The host says she has always maintained that Robinson played a role and was around campus, that she does not believe he had anything to do with the actual killing of Charlie Kirk, and that he could be guilty of tampering with evidence.
claims.investigative_direction: Compare the host's tampering theory against the charging documents and any evidence-tampering counts or investigative reports.
claims.transcript_snippet: I do not believe he had anything to do with the actual killing of Charlie Kirk, but I reckon that he could be guilty of uh tampering with evidence.

claims.label: Host Asks Viewers for Cemetery Follow-Up Tips at the moretips Address
claims.claim: The host asks viewers who know more about the cemetery or the Dairy Queen story, including police officers, to email tips to the moretips address for a cemetery follow-up.
claims.investigative_direction: Record tip volume and any follow-up in later episodes where the host cites emailed tips.
claims.transcript_snippet: Please email us more tips@canniswowens. com.

claims.label: Host Says Robinson's Car Was Possibly Driven by His Boyfriend Lance
claims.claim: The host says she believes Robinson's car was used around campus, possibly driven by his boyfriend Lance, and that she does not buy the story that Lance slept through the entire day.
claims.investigative_direction: Match Lance Twiggs' phone location and activity records on September 10 against the campus vehicle footage.
claims.transcript_snippet: possibly driven by his boyfriend, Lance.

claims.label: Host Does Not Believe Robinson Changed Into the Black Flag Shirt
claims.claim: The host says she does not believe Robinson ever changed on September 10 into a black long-sleeve shirt with an American flag, and does not believe he was on the rooftop.
claims.investigative_direction: Request the clothing evidence inventory and chain of custody for the black flag shirt and compare it to footage of the person who returned to campus.
claims.transcript_snippet: I do not believe a Tyler Robinson ever changed on September 10th into a black long sleeve shirt shirt featuring an American flag.

claims.label: Host Says Converse Sneakers Are Not Enough Evidence
claims.claim: The host says Converse sneakers are not convincing enough evidence to put anyone to death and that multiple students could have worn them that day.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain the footwear evidence report and any survey of other Converse-wearing individuals on campus footage.
claims.transcript_snippet: I certainly do not believe that the Converse sneakers are convincing enough evidence to put somebody to death.

claims.label: Host Says a Morning Meeting at UVU Is Plausible Before the Planned Assassination
claims.claim: The host says it is plausible that a morning meeting took place at UVU ahead of what she calls a very carefully planned assassination.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain UVU room reservations, access logs and calendars for the morning of September 10 to see whether any meeting occurred.
claims.transcript_snippet: I think there could have been a morning meeting that happened at UVU ahead of what was in my opinion a very carefully planned assassination.

claims.label: Host Believes Miss Noble Told the Truth About a Bald Man and Two Others in a Challenger
claims.claim: The host says she thinks Miss Noble and her husband were telling the truth when they said they saw a bald man and two other people in a Dodge Challenger early on September 11.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain Miss Noble's statement, 911 or tip-line record and the neighborhood surveillance referenced in the warrants.
claims.transcript_snippet: I think Miss Noble, uh, the neighbor and her husband were telling the truth when she said that she saw a bald man and two other people in a Dodge Challenger

claims.label: Host Suspects the Occupants Were Driving a Rental Car
claims.claim: The host says she suspects the people in that Dodge Challenger were driving a rental car, and that her best evidence is that no one, least of all the feds, can keep a story straight.

claims.transcript_snippet: In the video, Robinson is seen wearing a ball cap, a red t-shirt, light colored shorts, and Converse style tennis shoes.

claims.transcript_snippet: And he heads to Chick-fil-A, sits down, he eats Chick-fil-A, and then he goes to walk around campus to the wooded area where the gun will eventually be found.

claims.label: Host Says Hull's Account Has Robinson Sending a Wordle Score at 11:28 Then Changing Clothes

claims.investigative_direction: Compare the 11:28 message metadata and device location against the claimed off-campus timeline.
claims.transcript_snippet: He plays Wordle off campus, sends that score to his friends at 11:28 and then he changes back into his clothes.

claims.claim: The host says the account that Robinson changed into the black shirt with an American flag again and put on jeans has no evidence behind it and asks viewers to use imagination.

claims.transcript_snippet: And then he changes into that black shirt with an American flag again. Use your imagination. We have no evidence of that.

claims.transcript_snippet: That time gets adjusted three times across three different warrants.

claims.transcript_snippet: Actually, we can just assert that he simply was not shot by a 300 6. He potentially was not even shot at all.
